info.name: signals
info.description:
Signals sidecar (ai/signals): fast CPU signals for route-policy's evaluators -- PII NER, topic by nearest labelled examples, a jailbreak / prompt-injection score and language id, all ONNX / fastText on the CPU, pinned in ai/signals/models.yaml and baked into the image. route-policy calls it as http://signals:8000 inside ai_shared with ONE POST /signals per decision (ROUTE_POLICY_SIGNALS_URL, within ROUTE_POLICY_SIGNALS_BUDGET_S). No auth, like the classifier and the detector: from the LAN go through the ai/edge HAProxy on PORT_SIGNALS (default 8025) -- set the `signals` variable to http://<box>:8025; only clients in EDGE_ALLOWED_CIDRS get through, everyone else gets 403. There is no LiteLLM pass-through. The wire format is common.signals' (shared/common/src/common/signals/wire.py).

Workflow: GET /health (200 once every model is warm) -> GET /models (pins, vocabulary, caps) -> POST /signals with the task you are debugging. Send the nearest request twice: the first call embeds its example set (`warming`). Use fabricated text only: every request is processed in memory and nothing is logged but ids, counts and statuses, but a debugging session is still no place for customer data. Operator guide: ai/signals/SIGNALS.md.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `signals.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents its request body, its success response and every error status whose body is more than FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Any other error answers that `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails FastAPI's own validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem.

variable.description: Signals base URL. From the LAN: http://<box>:8025 (PORT_SIGNALS, published by the ai/edge HAProxy, limited to EDGE_ALLOWED_CIDRS); inside ai_shared: http://signals:8000 (what route-policy uses). No auth either way.
request_id sent with each POST /signals: logs only (route-policy sends its decision id). Logged when it looks like an id ([A-Za-z0-9._:-], up to 64 characters), otherwise as `-`.

request.description:
Prometheus text: signals_requests_total{outcome}, signals_request_seconds, signals_tasks_total{task,status}, signals_task_seconds{task}, signals_cache_total{task,result}, signals_cache_entries, signals_inference_seconds{lane}, signals_queue_depth{lane,queue}, signals_jobs_total{lane,outcome}, signals_example_sets{state}, signals_example_set_warmings_total{outcome}, signals_model_ready{lane}, signals_model_load_seconds{lane}, plus prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator's HTTP metrics. Scraped by the litellm stack's prometheus (job signals). See SIGNALS.md § Metrics.

#### Schemas

Response `200` (`text/plain`) — Prometheus text (SIGNALS.md § GET /metrics).

item.name: POST /signals -- all four tasks (what route-policy sends)

request.description:
NER over each whole text (gravitee-io/bert-small-pii-detection, windows of 256 tokens): per text {entities: {<type>: {count, max_score}}, complete, cached}, types from common.pii's vocabulary (email, phone, street_address, gov_id, card_number, bank_account, account_number, date_of_birth, person, location, other). A LOCATION span with a digit is street_address, without one location. Expect u2 -> person, street_address, phone; u1 -> person only (a bare name never forces in route-policy). Returns 200 {request_id, latency_ms, models: {pii, embed, injection, language: "<repo>@<rev12>"}, results: {<task>: {status, ms, texts: {<id>: <features>}, error?}}}. status is ok | partial | deadline | skipped | warming | error | unavailable (`error` carries an exception type -- also on a `partial` some of whose texts failed: the others still count -- or `loading`). No text, span or offset ever comes back. 422 {detail: "<field>: <rule>"} for a malformed request (an unknown key, a param the task does not take, a text id no text has, a task named twice, deadline_ms <= 0); 413 past a cap (20,000 characters per text, 200,000 per request, 64 texts, 1,000 examples of 300 characters, a 4 MB body). See SIGNALS.md § API.

#### Schemas

See *POST /signals -- all four tasks (what route-policy sends)*, the first request of this endpoint.

Nearest labelled examples (intfloat/multilingual-e5-small, the first max_tokens tokens): per text {neighbours: [{id, route, similarity}], routes: {<route>: {share, best, count}}, cached} -- example ids, never example text. `share` is the route's part of the top-k similarity mass (what route-policy's min_share reads). The example set is embedded once per fingerprint (at most 8 sets held): the first call answers `warming`, later ones vote. Returns 200 {request_id, latency_ms, models: {pii, embed, injection, language: "<repo>@<rev12>"}, results: {<task>: {status, ms, texts: {<id>: <features>}, error?}}}. status is ok | partial | deadline | skipped | warming | error | unavailable (`error` carries an exception type -- also on a `partial` some of whose texts failed: the others still count -- or `loading`). No text, span or offset ever comes back. 422 {detail: "<field>: <rule>"} for a malformed request (an unknown key, a param the task does not take, a text id no text has, a task named twice, deadline_ms <= 0); 413 past a cap (20,000 characters per text, 200,000 per request, 64 texts, 1,000 examples of 300 characters, a 4 MB body). See SIGNALS.md § API.

#### Schemas

See *POST /signals -- all four tasks (what route-policy sends)*, the first request of this endpoint.

Jailbreak / prompt-injection score (NeuralTrust/prompt-guard-oss-small): per text {score, windows, cached}, score = P(jailbreak) over the head and tail windows of max_tokens tokens (the larger). Route-policy logs it only (role observe). Returns 200 {request_id, latency_ms, models: {pii, embed, injection, language: "<repo>@<rev12>"}, results: {<task>: {status, ms, texts: {<id>: <features>}, error?}}}. status is ok | partial | deadline | skipped | warming | error | unavailable (`error` carries an exception type -- also on a `partial` some of whose texts failed: the others still count -- or `loading`). No text, span or offset ever comes back. 422 {detail: "<field>: <rule>"} for a malformed request (an unknown key, a param the task does not take, a text id no text has, a task named twice, deadline_ms <= 0); 413 past a cap (20,000 characters per text, 200,000 per request, 64 texts, 1,000 examples of 300 characters, a 4 MB body). See SIGNALS.md § API.

#### Schemas

See *POST /signals -- all four tasks (what route-policy sends)*, the first request of this endpoint.

Language id (fastText lid.176): per text {language, confidence, cached}; `und` with confidence 0 for a text with no letters. Inline: microseconds. item.name: POST /signals -- warm an example set (no texts)

request.description:
What route-policy sends at startup for every bound ruleset's example set: no texts, just the set, so a new copy embeds it before it serves. `warming` until embedded, then `ok` with empty texts. Returns 200 {request_id, latency_ms, models: {pii, embed, injection, language: "<repo>@<rev12>"}, results: {<task>: {status, ms, texts: {<id>: <features>}, error?}}}. status is ok | partial | deadline | skipped | warming | error | unavailable (`error` carries an exception type -- also on a `partial` some of whose texts failed: the others still count -- or `loading`).
